newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins two confidence votes in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins two confidence votes in Senate.

text.p: The Italian government won the first two of three confidence votes in the Senate (upper house) on Monday, which have been called to sweep aside opposition amendments blocking passage of the 1997 budget, officials said.

The vote covered two of three so-called umbrella amendments, which group together all the articles of the budget bill. Opposition parties boycotted the vote to protest against the deficit-cutting package.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government won the both votes by 166-0 with one abstention. Voting started immediately afterwards on the third and final confidence vote.
After the Senate has approved the budget, the package passes for further ratification to the lower house. Under Italian law, the budget must be approved by both houses by December 31.

The budget, which aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's deficit, is designed to enable Italy to meet some of the tough economic criteria laid down for countries wishing to join the single European currency.

Opposition parties support monetary union but have criticised the government for the tax hikes included in the 1997 budget as well as its plans to overhaul the fiscal system. They attached some 3,000 amendments to the budget bill in the Senate.
